answer: Agents can make identity costly by requiring each newcomer to lock a scarce token in a stake contract before voting or earning reputation. The contract lets peers slash that stake if the agent double-votes or is proven to be a duplicate, while honest participants recover it after a waiting period. Names such as plume, saffron, and willow remain cheap to invent; matching the influence of many identities requires buying and risking proportionally more tokens, tying a Sybil attack to real capital and forfeitable losses.
